info.title: Makimoto Transcription API
info.description:
Batched, server-side audio transcription. Upload an audio file, poll the job, and fetch the transcript once it is ready. Mirrors the Toku Transcribe contract.

Summaries and tags are derived from a transcription that has already succeeded: `POST /v1/summarize` and `POST /v1/tag` each create a job of their own, polled on the same `GET /v1/transcriptions/{job_id}` route.

The provider callbacks (`POST /v1/transcriptions/{job_id}/result`, `POST /v1/summaries/{job_id}/result`, `POST /v1/tags/{job_id}/result`) are intentionally not documented here — they are inbound webhooks from the providers, not client-facing endpoints.

servers.description: Production API (custom domain fronting CloudFront + WAF). All requests must go through this host — the raw API Gateway URL rejects requests without the CloudFront-injected x-origin-verify header.

tags.name: Postprocessing
tags.description: Derive a summary or tags from a transcript: either one of your completed transcriptions, or a transcript you supply directly, which need not have come from this API's speech-to-text pipeline.

get.description: Confirms the API is deployed and serving requests. Does not check the database or any other downstream dependency. Unauthenticated.

post.description:
Create a transcription from an audio file (**MP3 or WAV only**), sent one of two ways:

- **`multipart/form-data`**: the file in the request itself. The request passes through API Gateway and Lambda, so files above about 4 MB are rejected before they reach this API: use the second way for those.
- **`application/json`** with an `upload_id`: the file was first sent straight to storage through `POST /v1/uploads` (up to 15 MB). One upload makes at most one job: repeating the request returns that same job with `200`, so a request whose response was lost is safe to send again. A job that failed is not retried this way; upload the file again.

The job is submitted to the transcription provider and returns immediately with status `processing`; the transcript is delivered asynchronously and retrieved via `GET /v1/transcriptions/{job_id}`.

get.description: Returns the caller's jobs, most recent first. Supports pagination (`limit`/`cursor`) and filtering by `status`, `type`, `language`, `created_after`, and `job_id`, which compose with AND when combined. The cursor only encodes position, not which filters were active, so resend the same filter params on every paginated request or the result set can change partway through.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max jobs to return. Default 10, max 100 (values above 100 are silently capped, not rejected).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page. Not meant to be constructed or decoded by clients, its internal shape may change.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only return jobs with this status.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only return jobs of this type.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Only return jobs with this exact language value.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Only return jobs created after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: Only return the job with this exact ID. An exact match, not a search, a malformed UUID is rejected with 400.

parameters.name: flow_run_id
parameters.description: Internal use: only return jobs created as one step of a Flow run (the dashboard's visual workflow builder). A malformed UUID is rejected with 400.

post.description: The first step of transcribing a file too large to send through `POST /v1/transcriptions` (anything above about 4 MB, up to 15 MB). Returns an `upload_id` and a presigned form: send the file to `upload.url` as `multipart/form-data`, with every entry of `upload.fields` first and the file (field name `file`) last, before `expires_at`. Storage itself enforces the declared `content_type` and the size limit. Then call `POST /v1/transcriptions` with `{ "upload_id": ... }`. A file that no transcription claims is deleted within a day. Refused with `429` once the caller's minute quota is used up.

get.description:
Returns the job status. When `succeeded`, the `result` block is included; when `failed`, the `error` block is included.

Serves all three job types: `type` says whether `result` is a transcript, a summary or a tag set. A summary or tags job is polled here using the `job_id` its own POST returned, not the transcription's id.

200.description: The job, with `result` (succeeded) or `error` (failed) when available.

delete.description:
Removes the source audio from storage immediately and flags the job for scheduled deletion per the retention policy. Once flagged, the job reads as `404` on every route.

Accepts any of the three job types. A summary or tags job has no audio of its own, so for those only the scheduled deletion applies. Deleting a transcription does **not** delete summaries or tags derived from it: delete those by their own `job_id`.

post.description:
Creates a summary job from a transcript, supplied either as one of your own transcriptions that has already succeeded (`transcription_job_id`) or as text sent directly (`transcript_text`).

The second form does not involve this API's speech-to-text pipeline at all: the transcript may come from any source, and no audio, transcription job or quota is required. Only the first form can return `403`, `404`, `409` or `422`.

Returns immediately with status `queued`; the summary is generated asynchronously and retrieved via `GET /v1/transcriptions/{job_id}` using the `job_id` returned here, not the transcription's own id.

202.description: Job accepted and submitted to the summarisation provider.

post.description:
Creates a tags job from a transcript, supplied either as one of your own transcriptions that has already succeeded (`transcription_job_id`) or as text sent directly (`transcript_text`).

The second form does not involve this API's speech-to-text pipeline at all: the transcript may come from any source, and no audio, transcription job or quota is required. Only the first form can return `403`, `404`, `409` or `422`.

Returns immediately with status `queued`; the tags are generated asynchronously and retrieved via `GET /v1/transcriptions/{job_id}` using the `job_id` returned here, not the transcription's own id.

The tag taxonomy is fixed by the service and contact-centre shaped; it is not configurable per account, and does not vary with which input form was used.

202.description: Job accepted and submitted to the tagging provider.

apiKeyAuth.description: An API key created via `POST /v1/api-keys` (JWT-authenticated), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. This is an opaque `mkm_sk_...` key, not a JWT, despite the same `Bearer` scheme. For the service-call surface only (create/list/get/delete transcriptions, summarize, tag) — managing the keys themselves, and the JWT-authenticated `/v1/me/*` portal mirror, use `bearerAuth` instead.

file.description: Audio file to transcribe. Above about 4 MB the gateway rejects the request: use `POST /v1/uploads` for those (up to 15 MB).

language.description: Optional ISO 639-1 language code, such as `en`. Omit it to detect the language.

metadata.description: Optional JSON-encoded object echoed back on the job. Must be a valid JSON string.

flow_run_id.description: Internal use: attaches this job to a Flow run (the dashboard's visual workflow builder), if this job is one step of a Flow. Must refer to a run you own.

value.transcript_text:
Agent: Thanks for calling, how can I help?
Customer: I was charged twice for my subscription this month.

Forbidden.description: The job does not belong to the caller.

BadPostprocessingRequest.description: Body is not valid JSON, no transcript source (or both `transcription_job_id` and `transcript_text`) was given, `transcription_job_id` refers to a job that is not a transcription, or `flow_run_id` is present but not a non-empty string or doesn't refer to a run the caller owns (`INVALID_FLOW_RUN_ID`).

TranscriptionNotReady.description: The transcription has not succeeded yet. The same request will be accepted once it has, so retry later rather than changing it.

TranscriptEmpty.description: The transcript contains no speech to postprocess.

ProviderSubmitFailed.description: The job was stored but submission to the provider failed. The job is marked `failed` with `error.code` `provider_submit_failed`.

TranscriptionAccepted.description: Job accepted and submitted to the provider.

UploadRefused.description: No new upload can start: the caller's minute quota is used up (`QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, with `limit_minutes` and `used_minutes`), or 20 uploads from the last day are still waiting for a transcription (`TOO_MANY_OPEN_UPLOADS`, with `max_open_uploads`). Transcribe one, or start more later.

TranscriptionAlreadyCreated.description: This `upload_id` already has its job, from an earlier request. Nothing new is created, and this request's other fields are ignored; the body describes that job in its current status. If that job failed, upload the file again to try once more.

UploadCreated.description: Upload started. Send the file to `upload.url` before `expires_at`.

BadUploadRequest.description: Body is not valid JSON (`INVALID_JSON_BODY`), or `filename` is missing or longer than 255 characters (`INVALID_FILENAME`).

UploadNotFound.description: No upload with that `upload_id` belongs to the caller, or the job made from it has been deleted (`UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND`).

UploadNotReady.description: The upload exists but no file has arrived for it, or it is no longer stored (`UPLOAD_NOT_READY`): for example, the presigned form expired unused, or an earlier request for it was turned away and its file discarded. Send the file first, or start a new upload.

BadAudioUpload.description: No audio file provided (`AUDIO_FILE_MISSING`), the audio's duration could not be determined (`AUDIO_DURATION_UNKNOWN`), `metadata` is not valid JSON (`INVALID_METADATA_JSON`), `language` is not a string of at most 32 characters (`INVALID_LANGUAGE`), `flow_run_id` is present but whitespace-only or doesn't refer to a run the caller owns (`INVALID_FLOW_RUN_ID`), or, for a JSON body, the body is not valid JSON (`INVALID_JSON_BODY`) or has no `upload_id` (`MISSING_UPLOAD_ID`).

FileTooLarge.description: File exceeds the 15 MB limit (a multipart request is rejected by the gateway above about 4 MB, before this check; use an upload for larger files). `details` gives `max_bytes` and the upload's `size_bytes`.

UnsupportedAudioFormat.description: Unsupported audio format. Only MP3 and WAV are accepted; `details.allowed_extensions` lists them.

error.message: Unsupported audio format. Only MP3 and WAV are accepted.

QuotaExceeded.description: Accepting this file would take the caller past their transcription minute quota. No job is created. `details` gives `limit_minutes`, `used_minutes` and this file's `file_minutes`. The developer portal shows the same quota.

TranscriptionSubmitFailed.description: The job was stored but submission to the transcription provider failed. The job is marked `failed` with `error.code` `provider_submit_failed`.

JobStatus.description: Lifecycle of a job: `queued` on creation, `processing` once submitted to the provider, then `succeeded` or `failed`.

JobType.description: What a job represents, and therefore which shape its `result` carries: `transcription` a transcript, `summary` a topic and a summary, `tags` a tag set.

topic.description: Short label for what the call was about. Null when the model produced none.

meta_data.description: Generation metadata reported by the provider (model, batch size, timing). Passed through unread.

example.summary: The customer was billed twice for one subscription. The agent identified an uncancelled payment retry and raised a refund, quoting three to five working days.

tags.description: Tag category to selected values. Category keys are lower_snake_case.

JobError.description: Why a failed job failed, and what to do about it.

code.description:
Why the job failed. Match on this, not on `message`. New codes may be added; treat an unknown code as a generic failure.

- `invalid_audio`: The audio could not be decoded. Check that the file is a complete recording in a supported audio format, then submit it again.
- `provider_no_transcript`: The transcription could not be completed. Check that the recording contains speech, then submit it again. If it fails again, report the problem with the job ID.
- `transcription_timeout`: Transcription took too long and was stopped. Try a shorter recording, or split a long one into parts. If a short recording times out, report the problem with the job ID.
- `unsupported_language`: The requested language is not supported. Use an ISO 639-1 language code such as `en`, or leave the language out to have it detected.
- `no_summary`: No summary could be made from this transcript. This is a result, not a fault: retrying the same transcript gives the same answer.
- `no_tags`: No tags could be found in this transcript. This is a result, not a fault: retrying the same transcript gives the same answer.
- `provider_postprocessing_failed`: The summary or tags could not be produced. Submit the request again. If it fails again, report the problem with the job ID.
- `provider_submit_failed`: The job could not be sent for processing. Submit the job again in a few minutes. If it keeps failing, report the problem with the job ID.
- `queue_timeout`: Job waited too long in the queue without being sent. Submit the job again. If it keeps happening, report the problem with the job ID.
- `reconciliation_timeout`: Job exceeded the maximum time allowed without a provider callback. Submit the job again. If it keeps happening, report the problem with the job ID.

message.description: The cause, in plain words. Wording may change; match on `code`.

next_step.description: What to do about it. Wording may change.

docs_url.description: This code's entry on the job errors page, or the page itself for an unknown code.

provider_error.description: The processing service's own code and message, for Makimoto support. May change without notice; match on `code` instead.

upload_id.description: From `POST /v1/uploads`, once its file has been sent.

language.description: Optional ISO 639-1 language code, such as `en`. Omit it to detect the language.

metadata.description: Optional object echoed back on the job. A JSON-encoded string is accepted too, as in the multipart form.

flow_run_id.description: Internal use: attaches this job to a Flow run (the dashboard's visual workflow builder), if this job is one step of a Flow. Must refer to a run you own.

filename.description: The file's original name, returned as the job's `original_filename`.

content_type.description: The file's type. The upload must send this exact `Content-Type`, which `upload.fields` already carries.

upload.description: A presigned form. POST it to `url` as `multipart/form-data`: every entry of `fields` first, then the file as `file`.

expires_at.description: The form is refused after this: normally 15 minutes ahead, occasionally sooner.

PostprocessingRequest.description: Exactly one of `transcription_job_id` or `transcript_text` must be given.

transcription_job_id.description: One of your own transcription jobs, in status `succeeded`. Must be a `transcription` job, not another summary or tags job.

transcript_text.description: A transcript supplied directly, with no transcription job behind it. It need not have come from this API: another speech-to-text vendor, a chat log, a CRM export or typed notes are all accepted. Must be non-empty once trimmed.

flow_run_id.description: Internal use: attaches this job to a Flow run (the dashboard's visual workflow builder), if this job is one step of a Flow. Must refer to a run you own, a present but invalid value is rejected with 400 rather than silently ignored.

job_id.description: The new postprocessing job. Poll this id, not the transcription's. The pairing does not need remembering: `GET /v1/transcriptions/{job_id}` reports it back as `source_job_id`.

source_job_id.description: The transcription this job was derived from. Present on a `summary` or `tags` job created after the pairing began being recorded; absent on a `transcription`, which has no source, and on older postprocessing jobs.

input_text.description: The exact text a `summary` or `tags` job sent for processing: the flattened transcript (one `speaker: text` line per turn) when created from `transcription_job_id`, or the trimmed `transcript_text` otherwise. Absent on a `transcription` and on older postprocessing jobs.

result.description: Present when the job has `succeeded`. Which of the three shapes it takes is given by `type`.

audio_seconds.description: Audio duration in seconds. 0 for a summary or tags job, whose seconds were already metered by the transcription it was derived from.

flow_run_id.description: Which Flow run this job was one step of, if any - null for a Playground run or a direct API call.

trace_id.description: W3C trace id of the request that created this job, followed through every later step of the job. Quote it with the job id when reporting a problem. Null for jobs created before tracing was enabled.

error.description: Present when the job has `failed`. Same as on Get a job.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null if this is the last page.

total.description: Jobs matching the current filters across every page, not just the ones in `transcriptions`. Counted under the same filters as the list, so it changes as filters change, and is unaffected by `cursor` or `limit`.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable error code, e.g. `INVALID_BODY`. Match on this, not on `message`.

details.description: Structured context, present for some error codes only.

requestId.description: Identifies the request, for correlating with support.

error.message: Request body must be valid JSON.
